findings.confidence: High for source behavior; affected tenant population unmeasured
findings.title: Finance summary aggregates are bounded by display-oriented row caps
findings.trigger: More than 250 eligible orders or 100 active counterparties in the requested scope.
findings.observed: The service fetches capped order/customer/supplier sets and derives revenue and receivable/payable summary values from those arrays. The selected finance test covers payroll forecast proof, not overflow populations.
findings.expected: Summary totals and counts represent the complete declared population; paginated detail rows have an independent query.
findings.impact: Cash planning, aging, working capital and profitability can omit obligations or revenue and lead operators to incorrect decisions. No monetary loss or production incident was measured.
findings.likelihood: Conditional on population exceeding the caps; prevalence unknown
findings.rootCause: Summary computation and display data reuse the same bounded read arrays.
findings.mitigation: Organization filters and some explicit payroll proof states exist; they do not restore omitted rows.
findings.correction: Use scoped decimal database aggregates and separate detail pagination; bind totals to a consistent snapshot and explicit operational/accounting basis.
findings.acceptance: Fixtures with 251 orders and 101 customers/suppliers retain complete totals; pagination does not alter KPIs; export and detail reconcile.
findings.effort: 3–6 engineering days after the metric contract; production data investigation separately sized
findings.data: Recompute impacted views and identify exported/relied-upon reports; do not manufacture journal corrections for a read-model defect.

findings.title: Business Pulse includes draft orders and defaults the displayed currency to XAF
findings.trigger: An eligible location contains a draft order, or a non-XAF organization opens Business Pulse.
findings.observed: The sales read excludes only CANCELLED, sums the remaining order totals, and the runtime Business Pulse caller omits currency when composing output; composition defaults to XAF. Date boundaries also use server-local start/end-of-day helpers.
findings.expected: Recognized sales, currency and business-day boundaries come from reviewed tenant/source policy; drafts are not described as completed sales.
findings.impact: Operators may treat unfinalized demand as revenue or read the wrong currency, propagating incorrect signals into priorities and management decisions.
findings.likelihood: Conditional on draft/non-XAF/time-boundary usage; observed tenant frequency unknown
findings.rootCause: Generic order aggregation is reused for an authoritative-sounding sales KPI and runtime context is incomplete.
findings.mitigation: A blocked-state composer and composition test exist; the selected test supplies precomputed summary values and does not exercise source population or tenant currency resolution.
findings.correction: Reuse the existing analytical context work; define recognized event/returns/cutoff policy, resolve tenant currency and add source-to-UI fixtures.
findings.acceptance: Completed 100 plus draft 900 yields recognized sales 100 under the agreed policy; non-XAF and local-midnight fixtures retain correct labels and periods.
findings.data: Review affected dashboards/exports and downstream signals; retain source transactions unchanged.

findings.confidence: High for current field; user failure rate unmeasured
findings.title: HR approval requires a technical evidence-hash field
findings.trigger: An HR approver reviews an item through the approval inbox.
findings.observed: The current UI presents an Approval evidence hash input. The API accepts evidence data as part of approval; selected tests establish parts of the separation-of-duties and redaction contract, not usability of producing a hash.
findings.expected: The approver reviews understandable source facts; the server binds the exact revision and proof digest.
findings.impact: Users may abandon the flow, copy an unrelated hash or require developer assistance. This is a usability/control-quality exposure, not demonstrated approval forgery.
findings.likelihood: The field is present; frequency and severity of real user friction require task observation
findings.rootCause: An implementation-level proof representation is exposed as an operator input.
findings.mitigation: Domain decision eligibility and scoped/redacted inbox tests pass.
findings.correction: Resolve evidence server-side and show source revision, differences, decision reason and receipt while retaining maker-checker rules.
findings.acceptance: An HR user completes approval without manually generating hashes; changed evidence rejects stale approval; unauthorized/self-approval fixtures remain denied.
findings.owner: People frontend/domain engineering and HR controller
findings.effort: 2–4 engineering days, plus observed task validation
findings.data: No automatic historical approval rewrite; investigate questionable old evidence only if independently identified.

findings.confidence: High for missing key dimensions; cross-session disclosure not demonstrated
findings.title: Several sensitive query families omit tenant or actor identity
findings.trigger: Organization, actor, permissions or entitlements change while the QueryClient survives.
findings.observed: Payment and payroll keys use fixed prefixes (and limits/IDs); finance/offline keys include filters but no explicit tenant/actor. QueryProvider creates one client with useState. This review did not execute every identity-change path or establish whether navigation remounts/clears it.
findings.expected: Scope-changing transitions cannot render old protected results; result-changing scope belongs in cache identity with cancellation/removal where necessary.
findings.impact: Stale financial or personnel data may be shown in the wrong context if the client survives. Severity justifies early validation, but this is not a confirmed disclosure incident.
findings.likelihood: Depends on client lifetime and identity-transition behavior; unmeasured
findings.rootCause: Server-inferred authority is not represented explicitly in these client keys.
findings.mitigation: Server actions retain authorization and some keys have location/run filters; full reloads could clear caches but are not a complete demonstrated contract.
findings.correction: Trace every switch/logout/revocation path, then centralize scoped keys and query cancellation/removal; avoid retaining previous protected data across authority changes.
findings.acceptance: Same-browser two-tenant/actor tests show no old values during loading, errors or revocation; all impacted views refresh after writes.
findings.owner: Shared frontend/IAM owner plus affected module owners
findings.effort: 2–3 days to validate; 3–7 engineering days if shared lifecycle correction is required
findings.data: No data mutation required; assess exposure only if runtime reproduction identifies it.

findings.confidence: High for failing test; deployed defect not established
findings.title: Inventory idempotency-conflict test fails while recording anomaly evidence
findings.trigger: The focused test reuses a stock event key with a different payload hash.
findings.observed: Expected an idempotency-key conflict; received Business-event conflict evidence could not be recorded. The later assertions about stock mutation are not reached after the failed expectation.
findings.expected: A conflicting replay is rejected without stock mutation, and durable conflict evidence survives the required transaction outcome.
findings.impact: The current verification packet cannot prove this financial/stock retry boundary. A stale test mock is plausible; a real evidence failure must be ruled out.
findings.likelihood: Reproduced in the local fixture; deployed frequency unknown
findings.rootCause: Unresolved interaction between the fixture evidence client and the current anomaly-recording contract.
findings.mitigation: The operation rejects in the observed test; other stock and outbox checks pass. Rejection alone does not establish complete evidence retention.
findings.correction: Inspect injected versus independent evidence clients, update obsolete fixtures only if confirmed, and add an isolated PostgreSQL replay/rollback scenario before changing runtime logic.
findings.acceptance: Identical replay is idempotent; changed payload returns the intended safe conflict; quantities/ledger effects stay unchanged and the required conflict evidence is queryable after rollback.
findings.effort: 1–2 engineering days for diagnosis; any runtime fix and DB validation sized after reproduction
findings.data: No stock backfill justified by this test alone. If a real defect is confirmed, investigate source IDs and quantities before authorizing repair.

findings.confidence: High for catalog/search result; runtime/deployment scope unverified
findings.title: Catalog entries and actual workflow evidence need reconciliation
findings.trigger: A buyer or operator treats catalog status and route prefixes as proof of a complete workflow.
findings.observed: Commercial Agents is available, Presence is available and Content is internal in the catalog. Exact path-name discovery found no presence/commercial-agents/blogs implementation family; HRIS attendance and public landing surfaces do exist elsewhere. This is a search result, not proof of complete absence.
findings.expected: Every offered capability maps to a connected owner, route, data lifecycle and evidence-supported scope; aliases and deferred features are explicit.
findings.impact: False expectations, failed onboarding and entitlement confusion can damage trust. Commission liability or payroll scope must not be inferred from a catalog row.
findings.likelihood: Depends on which catalog promises reach users; not measured
findings.rootCause: Declared catalog scope and implementation naming/availability have not been reconciled in this review.
findings.mitigation: Content is already marked internal; HRIS provides related workforce/time capability.
findings.correction: Trace aliases and deployment flags, then document supported scope or restrict misleading availability. Do not build speculative CMS/commission systems as part of hardening.
findings.acceptance: Every advertised catalog row has a verified destination and owner, or an explicit unavailable/internal disposition reflected in UI and commercial material.
findings.owner: Module platform and commercial product owners
findings.effort: 1–2 days of discovery; approved product changes separately estimated
findings.data: No business-record changes; preserve existing grants and obligations when correcting availability.
